newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-BOYD SET TO RETIRE AT END OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-BOYD SET TO RETIRE AT END OF SEASON.

text.p: Rob Boyd, a 12-year veteran of the Canadian downhill team and considered the last remaining member of the Crazy Canucks, said on Saturday he would retire at the end of the season.
Boyd, winner of three World Cup races, announced his decision after failing to qualify for a place on the Canadian downhill squad at the world championships.
"I've seen enough omens, enough signs," said Boyd. "It's time to move on and let some younger guys move up."
Boyd joined the Canadian team in 1985, as the Crazy Canucks domination of the World Cup circuit was coming to an end.
But the all-or-nothing approach to the downhill made famous by Steve Podborski and Ken Read also made Boyd twice a winner in Val Gardena and in his home town of Whistler, British Columbia.
He remains the only Canadian to record a World Cup win on home snow.
"I have no regrets," said Boyd. "I got to win in my home town and stand on the podium in Kitzbuehel.
"Those were some of my dreams when I started racing."
Boyd's last appearance on the podium was a third place in Kitzbuehel in 1991.
Since then his career has been continually disrupted by injuries, including operations on both knees and his back.
Boyd arrived at the world championships looking to turn around a disappointing season which had produced just one top 20 finish in eight World Cup downhills.
But the 30-year-old skier injured his back while warming up for the first training run on Tuesday and was unable to earn one of four spots on the Canadian team for Saturday's downhill.

Boyd's last race will be in Kvitfjell, Norway on March 1 unless he can amass enough points over the final two events to qualify for a place in the World Cup finals the following week in Vail, Colorado.
